correctness.rationale: The unique singular point is forced by the triangular projective Jacobian. With \(n=d-1\), additivity of local intersection multiplicity gives \(\mu=(n-1)(n^2+1)\). An explicit lexicographic Gröbner basis for the Tjurina ideal has standard-monomial count \((n-1)(n^2-n+3)\). Their difference is \((n-1)(n-2)\). All hypotheses are stated over \(\mathbb C\) and \(d\ge3\); the isolatedness needed for Milnor theory is proved. The exact package verifier replays the algebra for \(2\le n\le10\) as a finite regression check.

value.rationale: The family is mathematically distinguished by being the unique sharp inverse-degree monomial Cremona family up to permutations. The exact Milnor–Tjurina profile quantifies the local deformation complexity of its unique singularity and exposes the structural transition \(\mu=\tau\) only at \(d=3\), with defect growing exactly as \((d-2)(d-3)\). This is a natural invariant of a singled-out infinite family, not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine normalization check.
